title: Normalize token timestamps after KMS rotation caused billing buckets to shift in Private deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
A subset of Private customers reported incorrect invoice totals for a rolling upgrade window (2026-03-02 22:00 -> 2026-03-03 02:00 UTC). Investigation shows token-level billing buckets were shifted by a timezone/clock-offset after a KMS rotation and container restart, causing many tokens to be assigned to the previous UTC day or zero-length billing intervals. This produced: inflated per-day spikes for some tenants, missing tokens in expected aggregates for others, and several customer support escalations requesting immediate credits and reconciliations.

Impact observed:
- 6 Private tenants across 2 customers had >15% invoice delta for the affected billing day.
- Billing pipeline grouped ~120k tokens into a single 00:00-00:00 interval due to identical timestamps from restarted token-signing process.
- Hosted/Dedicated customers unaffected; root cause limited to Private control-plane containers that apply local timezone settings during KMS key rollover.

Root cause (summary):
- During an automated KMS rotation on 2026-03-02, the token-authorizer service restarted on private control planes. The restarted containers accidentally inherited a host-local TZ environment (non-UTC) and a 3s clock drift caused by a sidecar NTP restart.
- Token issuance code records both issued_at (wall-clock) and sig_epoch_ms, but downstream metering relied on issued_at truncated to second precision and assumed UTC. The combination of TZ mismatch and sub-second truncation produced duplicate "00:00:00" timestamps for many tokens where sig_epoch_ms was not used by the ingestion job.
- The private ingest pipeline has a fallback that coalesces identical timestamps into a single bucket rather than de-duping by request-id, leading to large undercounts or misattributed counts depending on join order.

Reproduction steps (dev env):
1) Start private control-plane with TZ=America/Los_Angeles and NTP drift of -3s.
2) Run token issuance workload (100k short-chat requests) quickly across restart boundary.
3) Ingest pipeline job INGEST-TEST will show ~95% of tokens with identical issued_at second values; aggregation step collapses them into one entry for that second.

Immediate mitigations executed:
- 2026-03-03 03:20 UTC: Emergency hotfix deployed to private control-planes to force TZ=UTC in container env and disable NTP restart during KMS operations. (private-2026.03-hotfix-1)
- 2026-03-03 04:10 UTC: Backfill job launched to recompute per-token effective timestamp using sig_epoch_ms stored in audit logs. Script: https://git.company/repo/private-metering/backfills/repair-kms-timestamp.sh (PR #4217).
- Temporary customer-facing action: affected tenants received tentative credit estimates and an interim CSV reconciliation exported from the backfill. Account team sent emails and support tickets were updated.

Proposed permanent fixes (implementation plan):
1) Normalize timestamp semantics at source (token-authorizer service): always emit issued_at_utc_iso and sig_epoch_ms (ms since epoch). Update token schema (minor) and add contract tests. ETA 4d.
2) Metering ingestion must prefer sig_epoch_ms when available and use request_id as a stable dedupe key before collapsing identical second-level timestamps. ETA 3d.
3) Add CI gate to ensure any container restart path preserves TZ=UTC and to assert no sidecar restarts during KMS rotation routine. ETA 2d.
4) Extend observability: add a per-tenant "timestamp entropy" metric (percentage of tokens that share the same second value) to the Console billing dashboard and an alert threshold of >1% during normal traffic. ETA 2d.

Implementation notes and risks:
- Backfill accuracy depends on audit log retention window for some private deploys; two tenants with short retention required a best-effort reconstruction and will be handled via credit after PM review.
- Modifying token schema requires coordination with Private ops and version compatibility for older control-plane versions; we will ship a compatibility shim that populates issued_at_utc_iso from existing fields when absent.
- Security review required for changes that touch signature verification and KMS interactions. Security has been looped in.

Work items (current status):
- [x] Hotfix TZ override and NTP guard rolled to all affected private clusters (deployed 2026-03-03).
- [x] Backfill initial run completed for 4/6 tenants; verification dashboard show reconciled counts within 0.2% for those tenants (completed 2026-03-05).
- [ ] PR #4321: Token schema emission change (in review). Linked PR: https://git.company/repo/private-metering/pull/4321
- [ ] ENG task: Ingest pipeline changes to prefer sig_epoch_ms and request_id dedupe (in progress, assigned).
- [ ] Observability metrics and alert (blocked on ingest schema change).

Customer comms and next steps:
- PM (Lena Morris) to draft final reconciliation emails and credit receipts by 2026-03-13.
- For the two tenants with insufficient audit windows, Finance will offer manual credit after contract review.
- Postmortem and RCA to be published in Confluence (page link to be added) after final verification.

Logs / artifacts / links:
- Backfill script + logs: https://git.company/repo/private-metering/backfills/repair-kms-timestamp.sh
- Hotfix deployment runbook: https://confluence.company/ops/private/kms-rotation-hotfix-2026-03
- Support tickets: #SUP-1189, #SUP-1191, #SUP-1196
- Verification dashboard: https://console.redwood-inference/internal/dashboards/billing/timestamp-entropy

Acceptance criteria (for closing):
- All affected tenants either reconciled via backfill or provided a documented credit with Finance approval.
- Token emission and ingestion paths updated to use sig_epoch_ms by default, validated by unit/integration tests.
- New alert for timestamp entropy created and firing tests added to CI.
- Postmortem published and communicated to affected customers and SLT.

Owner notes:
- This is a high-priority cross-team effort: Engineering (runtime + ingest), Private-ops, Product, Finance, and Security are involved. Please update this ticket with progress and link PRs/Confluence pages as they land.
